[FIX]
```sql
WITH 
-- First merge all overlapping blackout periods into continuous blocks
merged_blackouts AS (
    SELECT 
        MIN(start_date) AS start_date,
        MAX(end_date) AS end_date
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            start_date,
            end_date,
            SUM(new_group) OVER (ORDER BY start_date) AS group_id
        FROM (
            SELECT 
                start_date,
                end_date,
                CASE WHEN start_date > COALESCE(MAX(end_date) OVER (
                    ORDER BY start_date 
                    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
                ), start_date - INTERVAL '1 day') 
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_group
            FROM blackout_periods
        ) t
    ) t
    GROUP BY group_id
),

-- For each account activity period, generate the operational periods
operational_periods AS (
    -- Period before any blackout starts
    SELECT 
        a.start_date AS activity_start,
        a.end_date AS activity_end,
        a.start_date AS operational_start,
        (SELECT MIN(b.start_date) FROM merged_blackouts b 
         WHERE b.start_date BETWEEN a.start_date AND a.end_date) - INTERVAL '1 day' AS operational_end
    FROM account_activity a
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM merged_blackouts b 
        WHERE b.start_date BETWEEN a.start_date AND a.end_date
    )
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Period after last blackout ends (if any)
    SELECT 
        a.start_date AS activity_start,
        a.end_date AS activity_end,
        (SELECT MAX(b.end_date) FROM merged_blackouts b 
         WHERE b.end_date BETWEEN a.start_date AND a.end_date) + INTERVAL '1 day' AS operational_start,
        a.end_date AS operational_end
    FROM account_activity a
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM merged_blackouts b 
        WHERE b.end_date BETWEEN a.start_date AND a.end_date
    )
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Periods between blackouts
    SELECT 
        a.start_date AS activity_start,
        a.end_date AS activity_end,
        b1.end_date + INTERVAL '1 day' AS operational_start,
        b2.start_date - INTERVAL '1 day' AS operational_end
    FROM account_activity a
    JOIN merged_blackouts b1 ON b1.end_date BETWEEN a.start_date AND a.end_date
    JOIN merged_blackouts b2 ON b2.start_date BETWEEN a.start_date AND a.end_date
    WHERE b2.start_date > b1.end_date
    AND NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM merged_blackouts b3 
        WHERE b3.start_date > b1.end_date 
        AND b3.start_date < b2.start_date
    )
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Case when no blackouts exist in the activity period
    SELECT 
        a.start_date AS activity_start,
        a.end_date AS activity_end,
        a.start_date AS operational_start,
        a.end_date AS operational_end
    FROM account_activity a
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM merged_blackouts b 
        WHERE b.start_date <= a.end_date AND b.end_date >= a.start_date
    )
)

-- Final result showing all operational periods
SELECT 
    activity_start::date,
    activity_end::date,
    operational_start::date,
    operational_end::date
FROM operational_periods
WHERE operational_start <= operational_end
ORDER BY activity_start, operational_start;
```

I'm trying to copy player statistics data from a temporary holding table into my main player stats table in PostgreSQL. The main table uses a unique identifier for each player, so I can't insert duplicate entries for the same player.

My initial approach was to use a loop to insert the data in batches, hoping this would be more manageable than inserting everything at once. I set up a process to repeatedly insert a limited number of rows from the temporary table.

However, this isn't working as expected. The process fails because it encounters duplicate player identifiers – it seems to be trying to insert records for players who already exist in the main statistics table, which triggers a unique constraint violation error. I'm not sure how to adjust this batch insert process to gracefully handle these existing records.

How can I structure my insert operation, possibly still using batches, so that it only adds records from the temporary table for players who are *not* already present in the main statistics table, thereby avoiding the duplicate key errors?

WITH RECURSIVE ExamSequence AS (
    -- Get all examinations ordered by id
    SELECT 
        id,
        'examination' AS type,
        1 AS qty,  -- Using fixed quantity since we don't have experiment data
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS seq_num
    FROM examination

ExecutableExams AS (
    -- Base case: first exam in sequence with initial "inventory"
    SELECT 
        e.id,
        e.type,
        e.qty,
        e.seq_num,
        CASE WHEN 5 >= e.qty THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_executable,  -- Using 5 as initial inventory
        CASE WHEN 5 >= e.qty THEN 5 - e.qty ELSE 5 END AS remaining_qty
    FROM ExamSequence e
    WHERE e.seq_num = 1
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Recursive case: subsequent exams with updated remaining quantity
    SELECT 
        e.id,
        e.type,
        e.qty,
        e.seq_num,
        CASE WHEN x.remaining_qty >= e.qty THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_executable,
        CASE WHEN x.remaining_qty >= e.qty THEN x.remaining_qty - e.qty ELSE x.remaining_qty END AS remaining_qty
    FROM ExamSequence e
    JOIN ExecutableExams x ON e.seq_num = x.seq_num + 1
)
SELECT 
    id,
    type AS resource_type,
    qty,

FROM ExecutableExams
